root_cause.text: In the qla2xxx SCSI driver, module unload could proceed while a fabric scan (`vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING`) was still active, causing an IRQ handler path (`qla24xx_sp_unmap` via `qla_async_scan_sp_done`) to free DMA-mapped memory when work allocation was suppressed by the `UNLOADING` flag, leading to an invalid `dma_free_attrs()` in interrupt context.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to also wait on `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)`, and the CVE text says the crash happened because “A module unload was issued which set the UNLOADING flag… the work item was not allocated and the mapped memory had to be freed. The free occurred in interrupt context leading to system crash.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the qla2xxx SCSI driver, module unload could proceed while a fabric scan (`vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING`) was still active, causing an IRQ handler path (`qla24xx_sp_unmap` via `qla_async_scan_sp_done`) to free DMA-mapped memory when work allocation was suppressed by the `UNLOADING` flag, leading to an invalid `dma_free_attrs()` in interrupt context.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()` to also wait on `(vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING)`, and the CVE text says the crash happened because “A module unload was issued which set the UNLOADING flag… the work item was not allocated and the mapped memory had to be freed. The free occurred in interrupt context leading to system crash.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Make qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() wait for active scans to complete before continuing.
intent_record.what: The wait loop in qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() was extended with an additional condition: it now also continues looping while `vha->scan.scan_flags & SF_SCANNING` is set. No other logic in the loop body was changed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will now treat an in-progress scan as part of the HBA-not-ready state, causing it to keep sleeping instead of proceeding until scanning has finished. This prevents the routine from advancing while scan-related activity is still underway.

grouping_result.intent: Make qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() wait for active scans to complete before continuing.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the core race in the root cause by making initialization/unload-related waiting logic block until active fabric scans finish, which prevents the scan/UNLOADING overlap that led to the invalid dma_free_attrs() path.

candidates.rationale: This unload check allows qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() to break out early during driver unload instead of waiting for an active fabric scan to finish, which matches the root cause where unload could proceed while SF_SCANNING was still active.

This loop governs the wait-for-ready path but, before the fix, it did not account for active scan completion. Continuing past this condition while scans remain active enables the unload/scanning race described in the vulnerability.
The existing wait condition only covered FX00_TARGET_SCAN, not the relevant SF_SCANNING fabric scan state. Missing the latter allows module unload to proceed while scan-related work is still pending.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unload guard allowed qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready() to exit early during module removal instead of waiting for an in-flight fabric scan to finish, which matches the race where unload proceeded while SF_SCANNING was still active and later IRQ-path cleanup hit invalid DMA freeing.

This loop controls the wait-for-ready logic, and in the pre-fix form it did not ensure completion of active scan work before continuing, enabling the unload-vs-scan race that led to qla_async_scan_sp_done/qla24xx_sp_unmap running in an unsafe teardown state.

The wait condition only covered FX00_TARGET_SCAN and omitted the fabric scan state SF_SCANNING, so the driver could continue toward unload while a fabric scan was still active, directly enabling the vulnerability.

In `qla2x00_wait_for_hba_ready()`, the loop now breaks early if `test_bit(UNLOADING, &base_vha->dpc_flags)` is set: `if (test_bit(UNLOADING, &base_vha->dpc_flags)) break;`. These additions are the corrective handling for the unload/scan race, so the vulnerable construct is not present in this version and the fix is already included.
